title: AttestArc verified knowledge entry
description: A single temporal, provenance-backed platform-knowledge claim — the VERIFIED (trusted) shape. This is what deterministic promotion (knowledge_compile.promote_to_verified) EMITS and what a released snapshot contains; the model never produces it directly. The model produces the candidate shape (schemas/knowledge-candidate.schema.json), which omits the trusted 'status'/'confidence' fields and the per-source publisher/type/authority; promotion assigns them. This schema describes the internal entry dict the runtime reasons over; on disk each entry is serialized as an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) concept file (markdown + YAML frontmatter) under knowledge/bootstrap/<domain>/<slug>.md, reconstructed to this shape by scripts/okf.py. An entry is trusted for reasoning ONLY after it passes the verification chain (scripts/knowledge_verify.py) AND its confidence is not 'candidate'. Secret values MUST NOT appear anywhere. Stable objects are closed (additionalProperties:false); host-specific data goes in the open 'extensions' object.

id.description: Stable knowledge-entry id, e.g. KE-gha-prt-checkout-default. Referenced by finding.knowledge_dependencies[].id.

kind.description: 'platform-semantics': how a platform behaves (defaults, trigger semantics); 'api': endpoint shape/response meaning; 'standard': an external spec (SLSA, OpenSSF); 'guidance': recommended practice.

platform.description: The platform or ecosystem the claim is about, e.g. github-actions, github, oidc, slsa, openssf.

subject.description: Short topic slug the claim is about, e.g. pull_request_target, cache-write, oidc-subject. Used by knowledge.py lookup --subject.

claim_key.description: Optional single-valued slot key for contradiction detection. Two active entries that share a claim_key and an overlapping applies_to but assert different claims are a contradiction (routes to needs_review). Use only for genuinely single-valued platform defaults, not for complementary facts about the same subject.

claim.description: The fact, stated plainly and testably. NOT a verdict about any repository. Contains no secret values.

applies_to.description: Scope conditions under which the claim holds. Absent fields mean 'any'.

events.description: Trigger/event names the claim is scoped to, e.g. ["pull_request_target"].

action.description: A specific action/API the claim scopes to.

version.description: Product/spec version the claim scopes to, e.g. GHES 3.12, SLSA v1.0.

valid_from.description: Date from which the claim is known to hold (platform-change date or first-observed date). Temporal lookups honor this.

expires.description: Optional date after which the claim must be re-verified. Absent means no scheduled expiry.

status.description: 'active': current; 'superseded': replaced by a newer entry (see supersedes on that entry); 'disputed': authoritative sources conflict (do not drive conclusions); 'retired': no longer applies; 'draft': not yet promoted.

confidence.description: 'authoritative': single authoritative source (registry authority >= 90); 'corroborated': multiple independent sources agree; 'candidate': unverified — MUST NOT drive a conclusion.

effect.description: The direction the claim moves an assessment when it drives a conclusion. 'mitigation': it lowers apparent risk / establishes a down-gate (e.g. a default is read-only, a checkout refuses fork code). 'risk-increasing': it raises apparent risk (e.g. a trigger carries secrets). 'neutral' (default when absent): neither. Used by the freshness gate: when the installed snapshot is stale (past its manifest expiry) a 'mitigation' or 'neutral' fact MUST NOT drive a conclusion (a stale down-gate could wrongly suppress a finding — route to needs_review), while a 'risk-increasing' fact may remain conclusion-driving (failing toward scrutiny is safe).

sources.description: Provenance. At least one source is required; a claim without provenance is not a knowledge entry.

supersedes.description: Ids of entries this one replaces. The superseded entries should carry status 'superseded'.

last_verified.description: When the claim was last checked against its sources.

compiler.description: Provenance of the extraction that produced this entry.

extensions.description: Open namespace for host- or tool-specific data that is not part of the stable contract. Secret values MUST NOT appear here.

source.description: One provenance record. 'publisher'/'authority'/'type' are DERIVED from the URL via the source registry (knowledge/sources.yaml), never chosen by the model, and 'retrieved_at' is always required as the temporal anchor. Pipeline-derived candidates are additionally bound to a fetched object — content_hash + retrieved_at, or a receipt_id resolving to a quarantine receipt — enforced by knowledge_compile.validate_candidate. In the in-package bootstrap snapshot a source's integrity rests instead on the attested pack hash in manifest.json.

publisher.description: Who published it, e.g. GitHub, SLSA, OpenSSF.

authority.description: Deterministic authority tier from the source registry. vendor-docs 100, vendor-changelog 95, vendor-repo 90, standard 90, security-org 80, research 60, issue 40, community 20, arbitrary-web 0.

type.description: Source class; maps to an authority tier in the registry.

retrieved_at.description: When the source content was fetched (ISO 8601 date or date-time).

content_hash.description: Hash of the fetched source content at retrieval time.

receipt_id.description: Id of a quarantine receipt (knowledge_compile.py) that carries the derived provenance for this source.
